## Telegram

```python
from roomkit import TelegramChannel
from roomkit.providers.telegram import TelegramBotProvider, TelegramConfig

telegram = TelegramChannel("telegram", provider=TelegramBotProvider(TelegramConfig(
    bot_token="123456:ABC-DEF...",
)))
```

Webhook parser: `parse_telegram_webhook(request_data, channel_id="telegram")` — returns `list[InboundMessage]`.

Inbound `external_id` and `idempotency_key` are `<chat_id>:<message_id>` because
Telegram message ids are chat-local. Malformed nested objects and invalid
coordinates are rejected at the webhook boundary.

- Inbound media (`photo`, `voice`, `audio`, `video_note`, `video`, `document`) parses to a `TextContent` whose body is the caption — empty when there is none, as on a voice note — plus `metadata["file_id"]` and `metadata["media_type"]`, and whichever of `duration`, `mime_type`, `file_name`, `file_size` Telegram sent.
- `parse_telegram_message(msg)` is the layer below: it reads a Telegram `message` into `TelegramMessageParts` (content, metadata, `message_id`, `sender_id`) and attributes nothing. `parse_telegram_webhook` is that function plus the ordinary attribution — the sender is `message.from.id`. Use the lower one when your identity model is not Telegram's (a one-bot-per-user deployment attributes a DM to the bot's owner), so that reading a `file_id` never costs you your identity model.
- Resolving that `file_id` to bytes belongs to the provider, which holds the bot token: `path = await provider.get_file(file_id)` then `data = await provider.download_file(path)`. Both return `None` on failure and log a warning that never carries the URL (every Bot API URL embeds the token). Telegram caps Bot API downloads at 20 MB and refuses larger files at the `getFile` step; `metadata["file_size"]` tells you before you spend the call.
- RoomKit stops at the bytes — transcription and storage are the application's call.
- `parse_telegram_message` also gives `entities` (a caption's markup comes from `caption_entities`), `reply_to_message_id` and `media_group_id`. None of them reach the `InboundMessage` — `parse_telegram_webhook`'s metadata is unchanged.

`TelegramBotProvider` is `TelegramBotAPI` plus the rendering of a `RoomEvent`. The API half is the Bot API surface an application needs around its sends, so it never writes a second HTTP client for the same token:

```python
me = await provider.get_me()                       # metadata["result"] = the bot object
if not me.success:
    ...                                            # me.error, me.metadata["description"]
await provider.set_webhook(url, secret=secret, allowed_updates=["message", "callback_query"])
await provider.answer_callback_query(cq.id, "Approved.")
await provider.edit_message_text(chat, msg_id, "Approved", reply_markup={"inline_keyboard": []})
```

Also `get_updates`, `delete_webhook`, `leave_chat`, `send_message` (plain text, no Markdown pass), `send_force_reply` (its `provider_message_id` is what a later reply is matched against), `send_chat_action` and `edit_message_reply_markup`. Every call answers with a `ProviderResult`: `telegram_<code>` / `http_<status>` / `timeout` / a safe transport exception class, and Telegram's own words under `metadata["description"]`. Transport errors never echo the token-bearing request URL.

Update reading is two levels. `parse_telegram_update(payload)` says which form arrived — a `message`, an `edited_message` (same shape, `edited=True`), or a `callback_query` parsed into a `TelegramCallback` (`id`, `data`, `sender_id`, `chat_id`, `message_id`, `message_text`). `callback_data` is posted by whoever pressed the button, so treat what it names as a claim to check.

`mentions_bot(msg, bot_username=..., bot_id=...)` says whether a group message addressed the bot — a reply to the bot, `bot_command`, `mention`, `text_mention`, or the handle as plain text. It gives the fact; whether that group answers only when addressed is your policy. `entity_text(text, entity)` slices by an entity's offsets, which count **UTF-16 code units** — a code-point slice returns the wrong substring as soon as an emoji precedes the mention.

## Discord

Discord has no webhook parser — it is a source + provider pair sharing one persistent gateway connection. `DiscordGatewaySource` owns the `discord.Client` (inbound); `DiscordBotProvider` reuses that client for outbound sends.

```python
from roomkit import DiscordChannel, RoomKit
from roomkit.providers.discord import DiscordBotProvider, DiscordConfig
from roomkit.sources import DiscordGatewaySource

config = DiscordConfig(
    bot_token="...",               # SecretStr
    intents_message_content=True,  # privileged intent — enable in the Developer Portal
    ignore_bots=True,              # drop inbound messages authored by other bots
)
source = DiscordGatewaySource(config, channel_id="discord-main")
provider = DiscordBotProvider(source)  # sends through the source's client

kit = RoomKit()
kit.register_channel(DiscordChannel("discord-main", provider=provider))
await kit.attach_source("discord-main", source, auto_restart=True)  # connects the gateway
```

Requires `pip install roomkit[discord]` (discord.py). The Message Content intent is privileged: enable it under Bot > Privileged Gateway Intents in the Discord Developer Portal, or every inbound `message.content` arrives empty.

- Recipient key `discord_channel_id` resolves the target Discord channel snowflake at delivery time.
- Capabilities: text + rich + media, `max_length=2000`, threading and reactions. `RichContent` is sent as an embed; `MediaContent` with an http(s) URL rides in the message content (Discord auto-embeds), a `data:` URI is decoded and uploaded as a file.
- Threading: outbound `channel_data.thread_id` (a message snowflake) becomes a reply reference; inbound reply references become `InboundMessage.thread_id`.
- Inbound parsing: `parse_discord_message(message, channel_id, bot_user_id=..., ignore_bots=True)` returns `InboundMessage | None` — the bot's own messages (and other bots, by default) are dropped, so echo hooks never loop. Metadata carries `guild_id`, `channel_id`, `channel_name`, `author_name`, `author_bot`, `message_id`. Override via `DiscordGatewaySource(..., parser=...)`.
- Reactions: `provider.send_reaction(channel_id, message_id, emoji)` outbound; inbound reaction add/remove events reach the source's `on_event` callback as normalized dicts (`action`, `emoji`, `user_id`, `message_id`, `channel_id`) — outside the message pipeline.
- Testing: `MockDiscordProvider` records `sent` and `reactions` without the `discord` dependency. ABC: `DiscordProvider`.

Runnable example: `examples/discord_bot.py`.

## Buzz (Nostr)

Buzz (Block's Nostr-based team workspace) follows the same source + provider pairing: `BuzzRelaySource` owns a `buzzkit.BuzzClient` — NIP-42 authentication plus a realtime channel subscription — and `BuzzProvider` reuses that client for outbound sends over the relay's HTTP bridge, so one Nostr identity serves both directions.

```python
from roomkit import BuzzChannel, RoomKit
from roomkit.providers.buzz import BuzzConfig, BuzzProvider
from roomkit.sources import BuzzRelaySource

config = BuzzConfig(
    relay_url="wss://your-community.communities.buzz.xyz",
    private_key="nsec1...",   # agent's Nostr secret (nsec or hex) — signs events, authenticates (NIP-42)
    ignore_own=True,          # drop the agent's own events (echo guard)
    auto_join=True,           # NIP-29 self-join (kind 9000, role=bot) on connect
    announce_presence=True,   # kind 20001 "online" on connect + periodic heartbeat
    auth_tag=None,            # optional NIP-OA owner attestation (buzzkit.compute_auth_tag)
)
source = BuzzRelaySource(config, channel_id="buzz-main", relay_channel_id="<channel-uuid>")
provider = BuzzProvider(source)  # sends through the source's client

kit = RoomKit()
kit.register_channel(BuzzChannel("buzz-main", provider=provider))
await kit.create_room(room_id="buzz-room")
await kit.attach_channel("buzz-room", "buzz-main", metadata={"buzz_channel_id": "<channel-uuid>"})
await kit.attach_source("buzz-main", source, auto_restart=True)  # connects + subscribes
```

Requires `pip install roomkit[buzz]` (installs `buzzkit`, a compiled wheel kept out of the aggregate extras). Hosted Buzz communities are closed relays: the agent's key must be a member first — claim an invite once with `buzzkit`'s `claim_invite`, then copy the channel UUID from the Buzz app.

- Recipient key `buzz_channel_id` resolves the target Buzz relay channel UUID at delivery time. Each source subscribes to a single relay channel — register one source per Buzz channel and bind each to its room.
- Capabilities: text only, `max_length=65536`, threading and reactions advertised.
- Inbound parsing: `parse_buzz_event(event, channel_id, own_pubkey=..., ignore_own=True)` converts a kind-9 Nostr event dict to an `InboundMessage` — sender pubkey becomes `sender_id`, the Nostr event id becomes `external_id` and `idempotency_key`, metadata carries `nostr_event_id`, `nostr_kind`, `buzz_channel_id`. Subscribe to other event kinds with `BuzzRelaySource(..., kinds=[...], parser=...)`.
- `provider.send(event, to=channel_uuid)` publishes a kind-9 channel message signed with the agent's key; the returned `ProviderResult.provider_message_id` is the Nostr event id. HTTP-bridge sends succeed even while the inbound WebSocket is mid-reconnect; the source reconnects with exponential backoff (1 s doubling to a 30 s cap).
- Testing: `MockBuzzProvider` records `sent` without the `buzzkit` dependency. ABC: `BuzzRelayProvider`.
- Presence: with `announce_presence=True` the source publishes kind-20001 `"online"` on connect, heartbeats every 30 s (surviving transient publish failures), and publishes `"offline"` on a deliberate `stop()` so the agent's dot flips immediately instead of lapsing by relay TTL.
- Owner control commands (`buzzkit>=0.3.0`): with `obey_owner_commands=True` (default), a kind-9 message whose trimmed content is exactly `!shutdown` / `!cancel` / `!rotate`, mentioning the agent and authored by the **proven** owner — the NIP-OA auth tag's Schnorr-verified attester, else `BuzzConfig.owner_pubkey` — is consumed before the pipeline (the AI never answers its own stop command). `!shutdown` stops the source gracefully; all commands reach the optional `on_owner_command` callback, which takes over the response when provided. No provable owner, or a non-owner author → the message flows normally (fail-closed). Replay-safe: a command issued before the source started is stale (relays replay recent history on every subscribe) — consumed without action; one issued during a disconnection is honored when the reconnect replays it.
- Inbound metadata carries `nostr_created_at` (unix seconds, the Nostr timestamp) so apps can tell live traffic from relay-history replay — used by `examples/buzz_agent.py`'s echo guard.

Runnable example: `examples/buzz_bot.py`.

### BuzzAgent — the lifecycle runner

`BuzzAgent` (`roomkit.providers.buzz`) turns a configured RoomKit app into a first-class Buzz agent: it attaches the sources (taking over their `on_owner_command`), installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers, optionally arms an `exit_after_inactivity` bound (seconds; default off; reaper on its own timer), and exits every stop cause — owner `!shutdown`, signal, inactivity — through one graceful path: `kit.close()` (presence `offline`, sockets closed). `run()` is single-shot, consumes the kit, and returns a `BuzzAgentStopCause` (`owner_shutdown` / `signal` / `inactivity`); exit the process with code 0 so supervisors never restart an intentional stop.

```python
from roomkit.providers.buzz import BuzzAgent, BuzzConfig

config = BuzzConfig.from_env()   # BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY (or NOSTR_PRIVATE_KEY) / BUZZ_RELAY_URL / BUZZ_AUTH_TAG — fail-closed
agent = BuzzAgent(kit, [source], exit_after_inactivity=7200)
cause = await agent.run()        # blocks until the owner, a signal, or idleness stops it
```

Runnable example: `examples/buzz_agent.py`.

Buzz huddles (live voice calls in ephemeral channels) are handled by the voice subsystem, not this transport: `BuzzHuddleBackend` (`roomkit.voice.backends`) is a `VoiceBackend` carrying huddle Opus audio for a `RealtimeVoiceChannel`, and `BuzzHuddleWatcher` owns the announcement-to-call lifecycle, watching the parent channel for kind-48100 announcements (`KIND_HUDDLE_STARTED` / `huddle_announcement_parser` in `roomkit.sources`) and bridging each huddle. See `examples/buzz_voice_agent.py`.

## Microsoft Teams

```python
from roomkit import TeamsChannel
from roomkit.providers.teams import BotFrameworkTeamsProvider, TeamsConfig

teams = TeamsChannel("teams", provider=BotFrameworkTeamsProvider(TeamsConfig(
    app_id="...",
    app_password="...",
)))
```

Features: proactive messaging, bot mention detection, reaction handling, conversation reference storage.

```python
from roomkit.providers.teams import is_bot_added, parse_teams_webhook

# Parse incoming Teams activity
activity = parse_teams_webhook(request_data)

# Check if bot was added to a conversation
if is_bot_added(activity):
    # Handle bot installation
    pass
```

## HTTP (Generic Webhook)

```python
from roomkit import HTTPChannel
from roomkit.providers.http import HTTPProviderConfig, WebhookHTTPProvider

http = HTTPChannel("webhook", provider=WebhookHTTPProvider(HTTPProviderConfig(
    webhook_url="https://api.example.com/messages",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ..."},
)))
```

`HTTPProviderConfig` refuses a `webhook_url` on a private, loopback, link-local,
reserved or multicast address when it is built. The client resolves the name
again at every send; a caller whose policy must judge the address actually
dialled (pin-on-connect), or a test that wants the POST to land in a
`MockTransport`, hands the provider its transport:

```python
provider = WebhookHTTPProvider(config, transport=my_transport)
```

A subclass shapes what is sent: `send()` posts `build_payload(event, to, text)`
(RoomKit's envelope by default) serialized, with `build_headers(body)` (the
configured headers and an `X-RoomKit-Signature` HMAC when a secret is set).
`config` is the provider's `HTTPProviderConfig`.

```python
class SlackWebhook(WebhookHTTPProvider):
    def build_payload(self, event, to, text):
        return {"text": text}
```

## WebSocket

WebSocket channels don't use a provider — they handle connections directly:

```python
from roomkit import WebSocketChannel

ws = WebSocketChannel("ws-client")

# Register a connection — room_id says which conversation this socket is for
ws.register_connection("conn-1", on_receive_callback, room_id="room-1")

# In production, connect to the framework
await kit.connect_websocket("ws-client", "conn-1", send_fn, room_id="room-1")
await kit.disconnect_websocket("ws-client", "conn-1")
```

One channel instance can serve several rooms, so a connection has to say which
one it belongs to: the channel delivers a room's events only to the
connections registered for it. A client holding several conversations open on
one socket subscribes to the extra rooms rather than opening more sockets:

```python
kit.subscribe_websocket("ws-client", "conn-1", "room-2")
kit.unsubscribe_websocket("ws-client", "conn-1", "room-2")
```

`connect_websocket(..., organization_id=...)` reads the room with the
organization first (RFC §17.2): another organization's room raises
`RoomNotFoundError`, no connection is registered and no `channel_connected`
event is emitted.

The channel's own registry is synchronous and reads no room.
`register_connection(..., organization_id=...)` registers the connection for
the organization: a room of another organization, or of none, delivers
nothing to it, streamed or not, whatever it is subscribed to.
`subscribe()`, `unsubscribe()`, `unregister_connection()`,
`kit.subscribe_websocket()`, `kit.unsubscribe_websocket()` and
`kit.disconnect_websocket()` take `organization_id=` too, and a scoped call
on a connection that is not registered for that organization (another's,
an unscoped one, none) raises `ValueError` and changes nothing, as does a
scoped `register_connection()` of an id another organization holds. Unset,
the calls act as before. A registration that changes the organization of an
id still known, to none included, drops the rooms it was subscribed to, and
a connection evicted after repeated send failures is forgotten as
`unregister_connection()` forgets it. A stream under way sends only to the
registrations present when it started: an id registered again since, a
reconnection of the same organization included, gets neither the rest of
it nor its `stream_end`.

Connection ids are one namespace for every organization: generate them on
the host server (a UUID per socket), never take one a client chose. A
refused registration tells that an id is taken, as a refused room id does;
an id no client can choose tells nothing.

## Phone Number Utilities

```python
from roomkit.providers.sms import is_valid_phone, normalize_phone

is_valid_phone("+15551234567")   # True
normalize_phone("555-123-4567")  # "+15551234567"
```

## Delivery Status Tracking

Track delivery status for sent messages:

```python
from roomkit import DeliveryStatus

@kit.on_delivery_status
async def track_delivery(status: DeliveryStatus) -> None:
    if status.status == "failed":
        print(f"Message {status.message_id} failed: {status.error_message}")

# Process status webhooks from providers
await kit.process_delivery_status(status)
```
---

## Identity Resolution

The identity pipeline maps external sender IDs to known participants. It runs as part of the inbound pipeline, after `handle_inbound()` and before hooks.

### How It Works

```
Inbound message arrives with sender_id
  -> IdentityResolver.resolve(sender_id, channel_type)
  -> Returns IdentityResult with status:
     IDENTIFIED      -> participant_id stamped on event, processing continues
     AMBIGUOUS       -> ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS hook fires
     PENDING         -> ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS hook fires
     UNKNOWN         -> ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN hook fires
     REJECTED        -> ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN hook fires
```

### Identity Hooks

```python
from roomkit import RoomKit, HookTrigger
from roomkit.models import Identity, IdentityHookResult

kit = RoomKit()

@kit.identity_hook(HookTrigger.ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN)
async def handle_unknown(event, ctx):
    # Option 1: Resolve to a known identity
    return IdentityHookResult.resolved(Identity(
        id="user-123",
        display_name="Alice",
    ))

    # Option 2: Challenge the sender to identify
    return IdentityHookResult.challenge(inject=InjectedEvent(
        content=TextContent(body="Please provide your account number."),
    ))

    # Option 3: Reject the message
    return IdentityHookResult.reject("Unknown sender")

    # Option 4: Keep as pending
    return IdentityHookResult.pending(candidates=[...])
```

### Custom Identity Resolver

```python
from roomkit.identity import IdentityResolver
from roomkit.models import IdentificationStatus, Identity, IdentityResult

class DatabaseIdentityResolver(IdentityResolver):
    async def resolve(self, message: InboundMessage, context: RoomContext) -> IdentityResult:
        user = await db.find_by_phone(message.sender_id)
        if user:
            return IdentityResult(
                status=IdentificationStatus.IDENTIFIED,
                identity=Identity(id=user.id, display_name=user.name),
            )
        return IdentityResult(status=IdentificationStatus.UNKNOWN)

kit = RoomKit(identity_resolver=DatabaseIdentityResolver())
```

### Manual Resolution

```python
# Resolve a pending participant to a known identity
await kit.resolve_participant(
    room_id="room-1",
    participant_id="pending-123",
    identity_id="user-456",
)
```

### Identity Verification

Identification says whose an address is; verification says the person writing
has proven it (RFC §11.7). With `verification_policy=VerificationPolicy()`,
every message of an identified sender carries `event.source.verification`, and
an unverified one fires `ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` (SYNC): `HookResult.allow()`
holds it from the agents (the room's transports still see it),
`HookResult.allow_unverified()` passes it, `block()` refuses it. The method
(a page behind a link, a code replied in the conversation) is the integrator's.

```python
kit = RoomKit(identity_resolver=resolver, verification_policy=VerificationPolicy())

@kit.hook(HookTrigger.ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED)
async def ask_to_verify(event, ctx) -> HookResult:
    state = await kit.sender_verification(event, ctx)  # identity_id, request_id
    if state is not None and state.request_id is None:
        request, secret = await kit.request_verification(
            state.identity_id, room_id=event.room_id,
            channel_id=event.source.channel_id, window_start=event.created_at,
        )
        ...  # send the link after the hook returns (the room is locked)
    return HookResult.allow()

# The integrator's page, after its own check:
await kit.complete_verification(request_id, secret)  # or record_failed_attempt(request_id)
await kit.revoke_verification(identity_id, reason="advisor")
```

On completion the held messages of the request's window are released to the
agents as the author's own turns. A held message whose delivery was cancelled
is released with no answer: when it is the last released, no agent answers,
and the earlier ones are not answered in its place. Its `delivery_key` names
it until then (`kit.cancel_delivery(key)`); its handle
(`defer_delivery=True`) cancels it only while its delivery set runs. The cancellation is written on the held event, so a release in
another process honours it. `ON_VERIFICATION_COMPLETED` and
`ON_VERIFICATION_ENDED` (ASYNC; `ended` is `"verification"` or `"request"`)
fire when it happens; a timer ends a verification at its expiry, and a
request left unanswered at its own (the identity then has none open, so the
next message asks again); `async with RoomKit(...)` re-arms the verifications'
timers from the store. A code reply
(`method="code"`) is consumed, never stored.

## Realtime Ephemeral Events

Ephemeral events (typing, presence, reactions) are not stored in conversation history. They're delivered in real-time to subscribers.

### Publishing Events

```python
from roomkit import RoomKit

kit = RoomKit()

# Typing indicator
await kit.publish_typing("room-1", "alice", is_typing=True)
await kit.publish_typing("room-1", "alice", is_typing=False)

# Presence
await kit.publish_presence("room-1", "alice", "online")   # online/away/offline

# Reaction
await kit.publish_reaction("room-1", "alice", target_event_id="evt-123", emoji="thumbsup")

# Read receipt
await kit.publish_read_receipt("room-1", "alice", event_id="evt-123")

# Tool call events (AIChannel publishes these automatically)
from roomkit.realtime import EphemeralEventType

await kit.publish_tool_call("room-1", "ai-agent", [
    {"id": "tc1", "name": "search", "arguments": {"q": "test"}}
], EphemeralEventType.TOOL_CALL_START)
```

### Subscribing to Events

```python
async def on_ephemeral(event):
    print(f"Ephemeral: {event.type} from {event.user_id}")

sub_id = await kit.subscribe_room("room-1", on_ephemeral)

# Unsubscribe later
await kit.unsubscribe_room(sub_id)
```

Each `publish_*` call and `subscribe_room` take `organization_id=` (RFC
§17.2): another organization's room raises `RoomNotFoundError`, nothing
published or subscribed. Unset, no room is read: a room id is published to
and subscribed to as given, as before.

### Event Types

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `TYPING_START` | User started typing |
| `TYPING_STOP` | User stopped typing |
| `PRESENCE_ONLINE` | User came online |
| `PRESENCE_AWAY` | User went away |
| `PRESENCE_OFFLINE` | User went offline |
| `READ_RECEIPT` | User read a message |
| `REACTION` | User reacted to a message |
| `TOOL_CALL_DELTA` | AI is composing a tool call (streaming only) |
| `TOOL_CALL_START` | AI started executing a tool |
| `TOOL_CALL_END` | AI finished executing a tool |
| `THINKING_START` / `THINKING_DELTA` / `THINKING_END` | AI reasoning, coalesced |
| `TEXT_DELTA` | A delegated task's answer text as it is written, coalesced (`text`, `round`, `channel_id`); opt-in |
| `CUSTOM` | Custom ephemeral event |

AI channels publish `TOOL_CALL_DELTA` with the tool name and cumulative
`arguments_chars`, never the argument content. A terminal frame with an empty
`tool_calls` closes every composition attempt, including cancellation, provider
failure, retry, and fallback; counts restart for a retry. The complete call
still arrives in `TOOL_CALL_START`.

With `AIChannel(publish_text_deltas=True)`, an agent's answer text is
published as `TEXT_DELTA` while it is written, for the code that delegated a
task to it (or a debugger watching the task), which subscribes to its child
room (its id is in `ON_TASK_DELEGATED`'s event metadata, `child_room_id`,
before the agent starts). It is off by default. The room's owner publishes it
only for a turn the delegation reads as its trace: the rows a child room with
no shared transport stores without a `BEFORE_BROADCAST` hook (RFC §23.3). No
other turn's text is published: not an answer in a room, nor in a task's child
room a transport is shared into, nor one another agent's message starts in a
child room, since a hook judges those answers and never this stream. A
subscriber therefore never reads an answer a hook blocked or redacted; a
delegation cut short may store less text than was published, what its executor
read ahead. The text is coalesced on `AIChannel(text_coalesce_ms=80,
text_coalesce_chars=256)` (`text_coalesce_ms=0` publishes every token), which
have no effect while the option is off, and flushed before a round's tool-call
events, so text and calls arrive in order. Joined, the texts are every round's
answer text (`round` tells them apart), where the task's result holds the last
segment only. Never persisted: the trace's stored messages are the answer. A
0.108.0 process cannot read a `text_delta` event (`EphemeralEvent.from_dict`
raises), so turn the option on once every process sharing the realtime backend
runs 0.109.0 or later. The room's owner decides what is published: a host
whose hooks filter answers needs every process that owns rooms on 0.110.0 or
later, since a 0.109.0 owner publishes every turn's text.

```python
agent = Agent("assistant", provider=provider, publish_text_deltas=True)
```

A turn's ephemerals (its reasoning, its tool calls, a custom one its channel
publishes, and what work it began publishes after it) reach a room's
subscribers only when the turn's answer reaches the whole room: the agent can
write, its binding's visibility is `all` (read at each publish, so narrowing it
mid-turn stops them at once), and the triggering message's
`response_visibility` restricts nothing (RFC §8.4). Subscribers are not bound
channels, so an agent whose answers are scoped elsewhere (a supervisor's
whisper, an internal agent, a read-only agent) publishes none of them.

### Read Tracking

```python
# Mark a specific event as read
await kit.mark_read("room-1", "ws-user", "evt-123")

# Mark all events as read
await kit.mark_all_read("room-1", "ws-user")
```

### Custom Realtime Backend

The default `InMemoryRealtime` works for single-process deployments. For distributed systems, implement `RealtimeBackend`:

```python
from roomkit.realtime import RealtimeBackend

class RedisRealtimeBackend(RealtimeBackend):
    # Implement publish, subscribe, unsubscribe using Redis Pub/Sub
    ...

kit = RoomKit(realtime=RedisRealtimeBackend())
```
---

RoomKit provides built-in resilience patterns for production deployments: rate limiting, circuit breakers, retry with backoff, chain depth limits, and room lifecycle timers.

## Rate Limiting

Apply rate limits per channel binding:

```python
from roomkit import RoomKit
from roomkit.models import RateLimit

kit = RoomKit()

await kit.attach_channel("room-1", "sms-out",
    rate_limit=RateLimit(max_per_second=1.0, max_per_minute=30.0),
)
```

Framework-level inbound rate limiting:

```python
from roomkit import RoomKit
from roomkit.models import RateLimit

kit = RoomKit(inbound_rate_limit=RateLimit(max_per_second=10.0))
```

## Circuit Breaker

RoomKit keeps one circuit breaker per transport channel. Five consecutive
failed deliveries (each after its binding's retries) open it: deliveries to
that channel are then skipped, without calling the provider, for 60 seconds;
after that one probe delivery goes through, and a success closes the breaker.
A delivery refused for having no recipient does not count. Each transition is
a framework event:

```python
@kit.on("circuit_breaker_opened")
async def breaker_opened(event):
    logger.warning("Deliveries to %s suspended", event.data["channel_id"])

@kit.on("circuit_breaker_closed")
async def breaker_closed(event):
    logger.info("Deliveries to %s resumed", event.data["channel_id"])
```

States: CLOSED (normal) -> OPEN (failing, fast-reject) -> HALF_OPEN (testing recovery).

## Retry with Backoff

A binding's `RetryPolicy` retries a failed delivery with exponential backoff
(`base_delay_seconds × exponential_base^attempt`, capped at
`max_delay_seconds`). An error that declares itself not retryable, or one
outside `retryable_errors` when the policy names some, fails on its first
attempt:

```python
from roomkit.models import RetryPolicy

await kit.attach_channel("room-1", "sms-out",
    retry_policy=RetryPolicy(
        max_retries=3,
        base_delay_seconds=1.0,
        max_delay_seconds=60.0,
    ),
)
```

## Connect vs Read Timeout

Every httpx-backed provider config in `roomkit.providers` carries `timeout` (the read/write/pool budget, sized for the slowest response) and `connect_timeout` (default 5 s, the TCP connect alone, TLS handshake included). Each adapter hands its client or SDK `httpx.Timeout(timeout, connect=connect_timeout)` rather than a bare float, so a host that no longer accepts connections is given up on in seconds rather than after the read budget: with one float for both, the kernel exhausts its SYN retries first, about two minutes per attempt, whatever the value.

```python
from roomkit.providers.polargrid import PolarGridConfig

config = PolarGridConfig(
    api_key="pg_...",
    timeout=240.0,  # read/write/pool: sized for the slowest generation
    connect_timeout=5.0,  # TCP connect alone (the default)
)
```

Applies to the AI providers (OpenAI and its derivatives, Azure, Anthropic, Ollama, vLLM, PolarGrid), the image providers, and the SMS, RCS, email, Telegram, Messenger and webhook transports. `AnamConfig.timeout` has no counterpart: it bounds the SDK's connect call itself, not an HTTP client. Raise `connect_timeout` on a link or a TLS-terminating proxy slow enough to need more.

Outside `roomkit.providers`, the same pair sits on `GrokTTSConfig`, `OpenAIVisionConfig`, `GeminiVisionConfig`, `GeminiTTSConfig` and `GeminiSTTConfig`, and is a keyword on `WebSocketAvatarProvider` and `SSESource`. Two read differently: `SSESource.timeout` bounds write and pool only (its read side is left unbounded so the stream survives idle periods between events; `connect_timeout` is what gives up on a dead host), and the Gemini providers (TTS, STT, vision) hand the SDK their own httpx client through `HttpOptions.httpx_async_client` rather than a per-request timeout, because google-genai flattens a per-request `httpx.Timeout` to its largest value (that client also keeps every SDK call on httpx when aiohttp is installed). The STT provider's Files API calls go through the SDK's classic path, which takes one value in milliseconds, so they carry the flat `timeout` and no connect split.

## Chain Depth Limit

Prevents infinite AI-to-AI loops. Default max depth is 5.

```python
kit = RoomKit(max_chain_depth=3)  # Stricter limit
```

When an AI response triggers another AI response, chain depth increments. Processing stops when the limit is reached.

What a turn sends into a room itself (`send_event()` or `process_inbound()`
from its channel, a tool handler or a `TurnHost` verb) is at least as deep as
the turn's response, so an agent that injects through another channel at each
turn stops at the limit too. Besides the depth, each cascade (an inbound
message or a direct injection) has a reentry budget of `10 ×
max_chain_depth` passes: its responses, its hooks' injected events, and what
the room's own work sends into the room (a hook, a parse, a delivery, a
turn). Past it, an answer or an injected event is stored `BLOCKED` with
`reentry_loop_cap`, and a message the room's work sends is refused
`reentry_loop_cap`, so a transport whose `deliver()` sends into its own room
stops too.

A speech-to-speech model (a `RealtimeVoiceChannel`, a conference's realtime
configuration) is held the same way. What its tool call's gate, handler and
hooks send into a room is at least as deep as the model's answer that issued
the call, and a text whose answer would reach the limit enters its session
silently, whatever brings it (a broadcast, `deliver()`, a handoff greeting,
`inject_text()`, whose text is at least as deep as the work it is called
from): the model takes it into its context and answers nothing. An `ON_TOOL_CALL` hook that posts at each call the model then
hears ends at the limit, and so does a hook on the model's words
(`ON_TRANSCRIPTION`), which runs at the depth of the answer it hears, and
one on its delegations (`ON_REALTIME_DELEGATION`), at the depth of the answer
that delegated (`examples/realtime_tool_observer_depth.py`).

A voice agent built from speech to text, an agent and text to speech (a
`VoiceChannel`, a conference's voice lane) is held the same way: the hooks on
what it says (`BEFORE_TTS`, on each sentence of a streamed reply too, and
`AFTER_TTS`) run at the depth of the answer they speak, so a hook that asks
the agent something after each of its answers ends at the limit
(`examples/hook_observer_depth.py`).

## Processing Timeout

`process_timeout` (seconds, default 30) is one deadline from the call's start
to its decision (RFC §13.6): routing, with the identity it reads, the router
and step 2's waits for the room lock, then the context build, the parse, the
off-lock checks and the locked gates. Past it, `process_inbound()` returns
`blocked=True, reason="process_timeout"` and `send_event()` raises
`ProcessTimeoutError`, nothing of the event written; the `process_timeout`
framework event names no room when the deadline passed while the message was
routed. A room step 2 creates is completed whatever the deadline, and step 2's
attach or record of a routed sender in a room that exists is bounded on its
wait for the lock only. The commit and everything after it (delivery,
answers, side effects) carry no deadline.

## Room Lifecycle Timers

Auto-transition rooms based on inactivity (RFC §5.1):

```python
from roomkit import RoomKit, RoomTimers

kit = RoomKit()

room = await kit.create_room(
    room_id="session-1",
    timers=RoomTimers(
        inactive_after_seconds=300,  # ACTIVE -> PAUSED after 5 min without activity
        closed_after_seconds=3600,  # PAUSED -> CLOSED 1 h after paused_at
    ),
)

# A room nobody writes to transitions when its timers are checked
room = await kit.check_room_timers("session-1")

# Batch check all rooms (call periodically)
transitioned = await kit.check_all_timers()
```

- **Activity** is the events the pipeline stores DELIVERED: each moves
  `timers.last_activity_at` in its commit. A record stored BLOCKED, a
  lifecycle record (an attach, a mute, a timer's transition), a
  `commit_event()` record and an instruction are no activity: a mute does not
  restart the inactivity timer. Inactivity counts from `last_activity_at`, or
  from `created_at` while the room has had none.
- **Pause and close.** An ACTIVE room pauses once `inactive_after_seconds`
  passed without activity, `paused_at` recording when; a PAUSED room closes
  once `closed_after_seconds` passed from `paused_at`. An ACTIVE room closes by
  timer only once it paused: to close N seconds after the last activity, set
  `inactive_after_seconds=N, closed_after_seconds=0`.
- **Resume.** A delivered event resumes a PAUSED room in its commit (ACTIVE,
  `paused_at` null), with no hook and no framework event.
- **When.** Every operation that reads the room's status under its lock (a
  message, `send_event()`, an agent's answer, an attach, a detach or a binding
  change, `commit_event()`, `update_event()`, `delete_event()`, `close_room()`,
  `archive_room()`) applies the transitions due at its instant first, so a
  message after a due close is refused as if the timer had run on time. A
  transition takes the instant it fell due, however late it is applied: a
  check long after both pauses the room at the first instant and closes it at
  the second, in one write. Each emits `room_paused` / `room_closed` (`reason =
  timer`) once stored, before the operation's own refusal (`room_closed` comes
  before the message's `room_refused_event`); its `ON_ROOM_PAUSED` /
  `ON_ROOM_CLOSED` hook fires once the room lock is released, its event's
  `SystemContent.data` the `threshold` and the instant (`at`).

## Delivery Status Tracking

Track whether messages were delivered to providers:

```python
from roomkit import DeliveryStatus

@kit.on_delivery_status
async def track(status: DeliveryStatus) -> None:
    if status.status == "failed":
        logger.error("Delivery failed: %s — %s", status.message_id, status.error_message)
    elif status.status == "delivered":
        logger.info("Delivered: %s", status.message_id)

# Process status webhooks from providers
await kit.process_delivery_status(status)
```

## Production Setup Example

```python
from roomkit import RoomKit
from roomkit.models import RateLimit, RetryPolicy
from roomkit.store import PostgresStore

kit = RoomKit(
    store=PostgresStore("postgresql://user:pass@localhost/roomkit"),
    max_chain_depth=5,
    inbound_rate_limit=RateLimit(max_per_second=50.0),
    process_timeout=30.0,
)

# Per-channel resilience
await kit.attach_channel("room", "sms-out",
    rate_limit=RateLimit(max_per_second=1.0, max_per_minute=30.0),
    retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_retries=3, base_delay_seconds=1.0),
)
```

## Framework Events for Monitoring

```python
@kit.on("source_error")
async def on_error(event):
    logger.error("Source error: %s", event.data["error"])

@kit.on("voice_session_ended")
async def on_voice_end(event):
    logger.info("Voice session ended: %s", event.data["session_id"])
```
---

RoomKit uses the `ConversationStore` ABC for persistence. Choose
`InMemoryStore` for ephemeral development state, `SQLiteStore` for an embedded
single-process deployment, or `PostgresStore` when several processes share the
same conversations.

## InMemoryStore (Default)

```python
from roomkit import RoomKit

kit = RoomKit()  # Uses InMemoryStore automatically
```

Data lives in Python dicts — fast for development, lost on restart.

What a store returns is its snapshot (RFC §14.4): a room, a binding, a
participant or an event read from it, the room, bindings and participants of a
hook's or a channel's `RoomContext` included, is treated as frozen, and changed by a copy
and a write. `InMemoryStore` copies a record once as it is written and shares
the stored object with every reader, so changing a read object in place
changes the store behind the write interface's back (a scratch copy is
`model_copy(deep=True)`: a plain `model_copy()` shares its dicts); SQL stores
return a new object per read, and the same code holds on all of them:

```python
from roomkit import RoomStatus

room = await kit.store.get_room("persistent")
await kit.store.update_room(room.model_copy(update={"status": RoomStatus.PAUSED}))
```

## SQLiteStore

`SQLiteStore` is included in the core package and uses only Python's stdlib
`sqlite3`. It is suited to desktop applications, edge deployments, and small
bots running in one process.

```python
from roomkit import RoomKit, SQLiteStore

kit = RoomKit(store=SQLiteStore("roomkit.db"))
```

RoomKit closes the database when `await kit.close()` runs. SQLite history is
stored as Pydantic JSON plus indexed query columns, and message text can be
searched with `await kit.store.search_events("invoice", room_id="support")`.

Do not share one SQLite file between RoomKit worker processes: SQLite
serializes database writes, but it cannot serialize the complete inbound
pipeline and its idempotency decisions. Use PostgreSQL with a distributed lock
manager for horizontal scaling.

## PostgresStore

Install: `pip install roomkit[postgres]`

```python
from roomkit import RoomKit
from roomkit.store import PostgresStore

store = PostgresStore("postgresql://user:pass@localhost/roomkit")
await store.init()  # Creates connection pool and tables

kit = RoomKit(store=store)
```

### Connection Pooling

```python
store = PostgresStore("postgresql://user:pass@localhost/roomkit")
await store.init(min_size=5, max_size=20)  # Pool sizing via init()
```

### Schema

PostgresStore creates these tables, among others:

| Table | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `rooms` | Room records with status, metadata, timers |
| `private_state` | What each room keeps for the runtime, apart from its metadata (the register of authors) |
| `events` | Event timeline with sequential indexing |
| `event_sequences` | Per-room monotonic event-index high-water marks |
| `participants` | Room participants with roles and status |
| `bindings` | Channel-to-room bindings with config |
| `identities` | Known identity records |
| `tasks` | AI-extracted tasks |
| `observations` | AI-extracted observations |
| `identity_addresses` | Multi-channel identity address lookup |
| `read_markers` | Per-channel read positions |
| `schema_version` | Schema migration tracking |

The tables live in the session's schema, `current_schema()` (the first schema
of `search_path` that exists). Two deployments may share a database, one
schema each: `init()`, `migrate()`, `dedupe_event_indices()` and
`drop_legacy_parent_index()` read, create and drop the tables, columns and
indexes of their own schema only, never a namesake another schema holds.
`init()` adds a column, or an index, only when its schema lacks it, and
seeds the per-room index marks (`event_sequences`) only in the boot that
creates that table. A boot on an up-to-date schema runs no `ALTER TABLE`, no
`CREATE INDEX` and no write of a row: it waits on no open reader or writer of
the tables, and none waits on it.

### Operations

```python
# Room operations
room = await kit.create_room(room_id="persistent", metadata={"topic": "billing"})

# Event storage and retrieval
events = await kit.store.list_events("persistent", offset=0, limit=50)

# Timeline query with filters
timeline = await kit.get_timeline("persistent", offset=0, limit=50)

# Participant management
participants = await kit.store.list_participants("persistent")

# Binding management
bindings = await kit.store.list_bindings("persistent")
```

### Full Example

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import os

from roomkit import InboundMessage, RoomKit, TextContent, WebSocketChannel
from roomkit.store import PostgresStore


async def main() -> None:
    store = PostgresStore(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"])
    await store.init()

    kit = RoomKit(store=store)

    ws = WebSocketChannel("ws-user")
    kit.register_channel(ws)

    room = await kit.create_room(room_id="support", metadata={"topic": "billing"})
    await kit.attach_channel("support", "ws-user")

    await kit.process_inbound(
        InboundMessage(
            channel_id="ws-user",
            sender_id="user",
            content=TextContent(body="I need help with my invoice"),
        )
    )

    # Data persists across restarts
    events = await kit.store.list_events("support")
    print(f"Stored {len(events)} events")

    await kit.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

## Custom Store

Implement `ConversationStore` for other backends (Redis, DynamoDB, etc.):

```python
from roomkit import ConversationStore, Room, RoomAlreadyExistsError

class RedisStore(ConversationStore):
    async def create_room(self, room: Room) -> Room:
        # A room is created once (RFC §14.3): never replace the one an id names.
        if not await self.redis.set(f"room:{room.id}", room.model_dump_json(), nx=True):
            raise RoomAlreadyExistsError(f"Room {room.id} already exists")
        return room

    # Implement all abstract methods...

kit = RoomKit(store=RedisStore())
```

What every store keeps alike (RFC §10.3, §14.1, §14.3):

- `create_room()` refuses an id it holds with `RoomAlreadyExistsError`, nothing
  written: replacing the room would re-home its conversation, another
  organization's included.
- `get_private_state(room_id, key)` and `set_private_state(room_id, key,
  value)` keep what a room holds for the runtime alone (RFC §14.1), apart
  from its metadata, which clients may read: a JSON object per key. The room's
  register of authors (RFC §6.4, §10.1 step 12) is the key `author_register`:
  its digests hash the room's id with each sender's id and name, and trying
  every phone number or name finds the senders. `get` returns the caller's
  own copy, `None` for an unknown room or key; `set` writes nothing for a
  room the store lacks, one deleted while it writes included, removes the
  key when `value` is `None`, and removes
  the copy the metadata may still hold under the key, in one write; the
  room's deletion takes its private state. The keys are the
  implementation's, and each reserves the same key in the room's metadata:
  the base class keeps the value there, and `set` removes the copy there, so
  only the runtime writes one there: the kit's `create_room()` and
  `update_room_metadata()` drop `author_register` or `_speak_queue_results`
  with a warning, as any `roomkit:` key, and write the rest. The store's own
  `update_room()` and `patch_room_metadata()` take any key: they sit below
  the kit's API, where migrations and the runtime write these keys. A register the
  metadata holds (a room stored before, or a process from an older RoomKit
  writing there) is merged into the store's at the room's next turn that
  names its sender (a BLOCKED turn does not): a register only adds, so the
  merge gives none of its ranks again. The base class keeps each key in the
  room's metadata, as before, and warns once: implement both to keep it
  private.
- `commit_event(room_id, event, *, target=None, activity=True)` stores the
  event and bumps the room's counters in one transaction. An activity commit
  (an event the pipeline stores DELIVERED) also moves `last_activity_at` and
  resumes a PAUSED room, in the same transaction (RFC §5.1); the framework
  passes `activity=False` for a lifecycle record, a BLOCKED record and a
  `commit_event()` record, which leave both. For a DELIVERED edit or delete the
  framework passes `target`, the target as the change writes it, which the same
  transaction writes; a target the room no longer holds fails the whole commit
  with `EventNotFoundError`. A delete's commit also marks every edit of its
  target `metadata.deleted`, in the same transaction: an edit holds a version
  of the deleted text. A host that soft-deletes a message itself, writing
  `metadata.deleted` with `kit.update_event()`, marks no edit: an edit the
  history holds without its message stays readable. Delete through the
  pipeline (a DELETE event, `send_event()`) or `kit.delete_event()`, or mark
  the message's edits too. An event whose idempotency key its source channel
  holds in the room for another event raises `IdempotencyKeyTakenError`,
  nothing written, its target included (RFC §13.4); the framework checks the
  key under the room lock first, so only a direct caller meets it. An event
  under an id the store holds is the database's own error
  (`asyncpg.UniqueViolationError`, `sqlite3.IntegrityError`).
- `update_room_if(room, *, status, paused_at, last_activity_at)` writes the
  room as `update_room()` does only if the stored room still holds that
  status, `paused_at` and `last_activity_at`, else writes nothing and returns
  `None`: a timer transition's compare-and-set, so a streamed row or a greeting
  committed off the room lock is never overwritten by a stale close or pause.
  The shipped stores hold the room's row from the comparison to the write;
  the default reads, compares and writes, and is not atomic.
- `write_change_target(room_id, target)` writes the target of an edit or a
  delete the persistence policy keeps out of the timeline: the target's row
  alone, no row of the change, and when the target is now deleted every edit
  of it marked deleted, in one transaction. A target the room no longer holds
  raises `EventNotFoundError`. Its default writes through `update_event()` and
  is not atomic.
- `delete_event(room_id, event_id, cascade_replies=True)` is a hard delete: the
  event, its thread replies unless told not to, and the edits and deletes of
  every event it removes, in one transaction, their idempotency keys released.
  It returns the removed events as stored: the root, its replies, then the
  changes, each in index order.
- The routing lookups (RFC §10.4, §14.1) answer the newest room, the most
  recently created, the greatest id on a tie, among the rooms a
  `RoomFilter(statuses, organization_id)` reads:
  `find_room_id_by_binding(channel_id, participant_id, identity_id,
  room_filter, *, recipient_key=None)` finds a binding naming the address or
  the identity, or naming no one and not `group` with the address as its
  recipient under `recipient_key` (SQLite reads an integer recipient beyond
  64 bits as a real number and does not find it; the other stores do);
  `find_room_id_by_participant(channel_id,
  participant_id, identity_id, room_filter)` a participant reached through the
  channel whose id or identity is one of the names;
  `find_room_ids_by_channel(channel_id, room_filter, limit, *, group=None)`
  the rooms bound to the channel, oldest first, `group` keeping a group
  binding's rooms or the others. The base class falls back to scans.
- `check_idempotency(room_id, key, *, channel_id)` and
  `get_event_by_idempotency_key(room_id, key, *, channel_id)` look a key up
  within its source channel, or with `channel_id=None` within the whole room
  (the lowest index first), as a proactive delivery's key is.
- `record_delivery_results(room_id, event_id, results)` writes a delivery set's
  outcome on the event as stored, replacing the map, that field alone, so an
  edit or a delete committed while the delivery ran stands. An event is
  committed with the `delivery_results` it brings; once stored, this is the
  one write of `delivery_results`: `update_event()` and a change's target
  (`commit_event(target=)`, `write_change_target()`) keep the stored results,
  whatever the copy they write carries. Its default reads the event and
  writes it back through `update_event()` (the framework calls it under the
  room lock), which works for a store whose `update_event()` writes the row
  as given; a store that keeps the results there overrides
  `record_delivery_results()`, and the default, reading the event back,
  raises `NotImplementedError` saying so rather than record nothing (the
  framework logs it as a delivery record it could not write).
---

RoomKit provides mock implementations for every pluggable component: AI providers, voice backends, pipeline stages, identity resolvers, and telemetry.

## Test Setup

```bash
pip install roomkit[dev]
uv run pytest              # Run all tests
uv run pytest tests/test_framework.py -v  # Specific file
```

Configuration in `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"  # No @pytest.mark.asyncio needed
```

## Basic Test Pattern

```python
from roomkit import RoomKit, InboundMessage, TextContent, WebSocketChannel


class TestMyFeature:
    async def test_message_delivery(self) -> None:
        kit = RoomKit()

        alice = WebSocketChannel("ws-alice")
        bob = WebSocketChannel("ws-bob")
        kit.register_channel(alice)
        kit.register_channel(bob)

        await kit.create_room(room_id="test-room")
        await kit.attach_channel("test-room", "ws-alice")
        await kit.attach_channel("test-room", "ws-bob")

        bob_inbox: list = []
        async def on_recv(_conn: str, event) -> None:
            bob_inbox.append(event)

        bob.register_connection("bob-conn", on_recv, room_id="test-room")

        result = await kit.process_inbound(
            InboundMessage(
                channel_id="ws-alice",
                sender_id="alice",
                content=TextContent(body="Hello"),
            )
        )

        assert not result.blocked
        # The room delivers to the other channels, never back to the sender's
        assert len(bob_inbox) == 1
        assert bob_inbox[0].content.body == "Hello"
```

## Recording Transport and Echo Agent

`roomkit.testing` gives a test or an example the two channels it needs to see
a room work without a provider, as roomkit-rs's `roomkit::testing` does:

```python
from roomkit import ChannelCategory, ChannelType, RoomKit
from roomkit.testing import EchoAgent, RecordingTransport

kit = RoomKit()
ws = RecordingTransport("ws", ChannelType.WEBSOCKET)
kit.register_channel(ws)
kit.register_channel(EchoAgent("echo", "You said: ", quote=True))
await kit.create_room(room_id="r1")
await kit.attach_channel("r1", "ws")
await kit.attach_channel("r1", "echo", category=ChannelCategory.INTELLIGENCE)
# ... a message into the room ...
assert ws.texts == ["Hello.", "You said: Hello."]
```

- `RecordingTransport(channel_id, channel_type, *, capabilities=None)` records
  every event delivered to it: `deliveries` holds each one as a
  `Delivery(event, text)`, the event as transcoded for it and its text as a
  person on the transport reads it; `texts` the texts alone. It needs no
  recipient, and addresses its senders as its type does (an SMS one in E.164).
  `capabilities` are those it declares: one that edits natively receives an
  edit as it is.
- `EchoAgent(channel_id, reply, *, quote=False)` answers every event it is
  asked with `reply`, followed by the event's text when `quote` is set.

## Mock AI Provider

```python
from roomkit.providers.ai import MockAIProvider
from roomkit import AIChannel, ChannelCategory

# Responds with pre-configured messages in order
provider = MockAIProvider(responses=["Response 1", "Response 2"])

ai = AIChannel("ai", provider=provider)
kit.register_channel(ai)
await kit.attach_channel("room", "ai", category=ChannelCategory.INTELLIGENCE)

# After processing, check what the AI was called with:
assert len(provider.calls) == 1
last_call = provider.calls[-1]
print(last_call.system_prompt)
print(last_call.temperature)
print([t.name for t in last_call.tools])
```

## Voice Test Bench

`roomkit.voice.testing` replaces frame-by-frame injection and `asyncio.sleep`
with a simulated phone and a hook timeline. `ScenarioVoiceBackend` extends
`MockVoiceBackend`: `play()` cuts a WAV or a `PCMAudio` clip into 20 ms frames
delivered at a transport's cadence (or back to back with `realtime=False`) and
captures what the bot sends per session. `VoiceTrace` records when each voice
hook fired, so a test waits for the hook it needs and reads the turn's order and
latencies off the timeline.

```python
from roomkit import HookTrigger, RoomKit, ScenarioVoiceBackend, VoiceTrace
from roomkit.voice.testing import read_wav, tone, write_wav

backend = ScenarioVoiceBackend()
kit = RoomKit(stt=stt, tts=tts, voice=backend)
trace = VoiceTrace(kit)                     # before the first session
# ... register the VoiceChannel, create the room, join the session ...

await backend.play(session, tone(300), realtime=False)   # or a WAV path
heard = await trace.wait_for(HookTrigger.ON_TRANSCRIPTION, timeout=2)
await trace.wait_for(HookTrigger.AFTER_TTS)              # TimeoutError names what did fire

speech_end = trace.first(HookTrigger.ON_SPEECH_END)
assert speech_end is not None
trace.elapsed_ms(speech_end, heard)                      # STT latency, ms
trace.sequence()                                         # the hooks, in order
backend.write_capture(session, "reports/bot.wav")        # what the bot said
```

`ScenarioVoiceBackend(mute_mic_during_playback=True)` drops the caller's frames
while the bot is speaking, as `LocalAudioBackend` does by default;
`is_speaking(session)` holds for as long as the bot's audio lasts. Use it to
test what a continuous STT stream does when the audio stops mid-session.

`read_wav`, `write_wav`, `pcm_frames`, `silence` and `tone` are the stdlib WAV
and PCM helpers around `PCMAudio`. Example: `examples/voice_scenario_backend.py`.

## Testing Hooks

```python
from roomkit import HookTrigger, HookResult, HookExecution

async def test_hook_blocks_message() -> None:
    kit = RoomKit()
    ws = WebSocketChannel("ws")
    kit.register_channel(ws)

    await kit.create_room(room_id="r")
    await kit.attach_channel("r", "ws")

    @kit.hook(HookTrigger.BEFORE_BROADCAST)
    async def blocker(event, ctx):
        return HookResult.block("blocked")

    result = await kit.process_inbound(
        InboundMessage(
            channel_id="ws",
            sender_id="user",
            content=TextContent(body="test"),
        )
    )

    assert result.blocked
    assert result.reason == "blocked"
```

## Testing Voice Pipeline

```python
from roomkit import VoiceChannel
from roomkit.voice.pipeline import AudioPipelineConfig, MockVADProvider, VADEvent, VADEventType
from roomkit.voice.stt import MockSTTProvider
from roomkit.voice.tts import MockTTSProvider
from roomkit.voice.backends import MockVoiceBackend
from roomkit.voice import AudioFrame

async def test_voice_pipeline() -> None:
    kit = RoomKit()

    backend = MockVoiceBackend()
    stt = MockSTTProvider(transcripts=["Hello"])
    tts = MockTTSProvider()
    vad = MockVADProvider(events=[
        VADEvent(type=VADEventType.SPEECH_START),
        None,
        VADEvent(type=VADEventType.SPEECH_END, audio_bytes=b"audio"),
    ])

    voice = VoiceChannel(
        "voice", stt=stt, tts=tts, backend=backend,
        pipeline=AudioPipelineConfig(vad=vad),
    )
    kit.register_channel(voice)

    await kit.create_room(room_id="call")
    await kit.attach_channel("call", "voice")

    # Simulate audio input
    frame = AudioFrame(data=b"\x00" * 320, sample_rate=16000)
    backend.simulate_audio_received(None, frame)
```

## Testing Orchestration

```python
from roomkit import Agent, Pipeline, RoomKit, WebSocketChannel
from roomkit.providers.ai import MockAIProvider

async def test_pipeline_orchestration() -> None:
    agent1 = Agent("a1", provider=MockAIProvider(responses=["Transferring..."]))
    agent2 = Agent("a2", provider=MockAIProvider(responses=["Resolved!"]))

    kit = RoomKit(orchestration=Pipeline(agents=[agent1, agent2]))

    ws = WebSocketChannel("ws")
    kit.register_channel(ws)

    await kit.create_room(room_id="test")
    await kit.attach_channel("test", "ws")

    # First message goes to agent1
    result = await kit.process_inbound(
        InboundMessage(channel_id="ws", sender_id="user", content=TextContent(body="Help"))
    )
    assert not result.blocked
```

# Never mutate models directly — always use model_copy

---

RoomKit exports **348 symbols** from `roomkit`. Providers and voice types import from subpackages.

## Top-Level Imports (`from roomkit import ...`)

### Framework

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `RoomKit` | Central orchestrator — rooms, channels, hooks, storage |
| `RoomKitConsole` | Full-screen terminal dashboard for voice agent development (optional, requires `rich`) |
| `__version__` | Package version string |
| `content_logging_enabled` | Whether raw message content may be written to logs (default False) |
| `set_content_logging` | Enable/disable process-wide logging of raw message content |

### Channels

| `VideoChannel` | Video channel with vision pipeline |

| Symbol | Description |

| `Tool` | Base class for tool definitions |
| `ToolHandler` | Tool handler type for realtime voice |

| `RoleOverride` | Per-role tool policy override |
| `ToolCallCallback` | Callback type for tool call events |
| `ToolCallEvent` | Tool call event model |
| `ToolCallContent` | Content for TOOL_CALL_START and TOOL_CALL_END events |
| `AIGenerationEvent` | Payload for BEFORE_AI_GENERATION hooks, before AI provider invocation |
| `EmptyEventDescriber` | `AIChannel(describe_empty_event=...)`: an event whose content extracts to nothing, in; the text the transcript reads for it, or `None` to omit it, out |
| `MediaResolver` | `RoomKit(media_resolver=...)`: a referenced `MediaContent` (`<scheme>://…`) and its room id, in; the media's bytes, or `None` when this room may not show it, out (RFC §6.4) |
| `AttachedMedia` | `RoomKit(attached_media=...)`: an event in; the `MediaContent`s its application keeps beside its content out, the same ones in the same order each time, which every AI channel reads after the event's own content (RFC §6.4) |
| `ContinuationPolicy` | `AIChannel(continuation=...)`: the text of a round the model ended itself without a call, in; the instruction to go on, or `None`, out (RFC §6.4) |
| `ToolRoundEvent` | Payload for AFTER_TOOL_ROUND hooks, between two rounds of a tool loop: the round's calls and results, the turn's toolset, `withdraw()` and `add_message()` |
| `AIResponseEvent` | Payload for ON_AI_RESPONSE hooks, after AI generation completes |
| `BeforeGenerationCallback` | Async callback type receiving AIGenerationEvent |
| `AfterResponseCallback` | Async callback type receiving AIResponseEvent |
| `HumanInputHandler` | Manages pending human input requests |
| `HumanInputToolHandler` | ToolHandler wrapper that blocks on human input for specified tools |
| `PendingInput` | A pending human input request |
| `PendingInputEvent` | Event fired through ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED hooks |
| `PendingInputStatus` | Status of a pending human input request |

### Delivery

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `DeliveryStrategy` | ABC controlling when and how content is delivered to a channel |
| `Immediate` | Deliver now; on voice, after the playback under way |
| `Queued` | Add to queue, deliver at the next idle window |
| `WaitForIdle` | Wait for TTS/speech to finish, then send |
| `DeliveryBackend` | ABC for persistent delivery queue backends |
| `DeliveryItem` | Serializable delivery request — the unit of work in the queue |
| `DeliveryItemStatus` | Lifecycle status of a delivery item |
| `InMemoryDeliveryBackend` | Asyncio-queue delivery backend (single process, no persistence) |
| `TurnBackend` | ABC for what carries an intelligence channel's turns between the room owner and an executor (RFC §10.6) |
| `InMemoryTurnBackend` | Default turn backend: in this process, every message serialized but a request's events, which reach the executor as they are |
| `RedisTurnBackend` | Turn backend across processes (`pip install roomkit[redis]`): one per process on a shared Redis and store; an executor declared with `hosts={...}` takes turns from every process, beating from a thread; a killed executor fails its turn with `executor_lost` |
| `TurnExecutor` | Builds a channel and runs its turns; the kit owns one reading its registered channels. One a host builds (`TurnExecutor(build_channel, hosts={...}, store=, media_resolver=, attached_media=, telemetry=, error_classes=)`, `hosts` the set of channel ids it runs, or a predicate for its own process only; with an `OpenTelemetryProvider` as `telemetry=`, a turn from another process continues the owner's trace) builds each channel once, wires it as the kit wires the ones it registers (its hooks fire, what the channel publishes during a turn crosses as `ephemeral` / `framework_event` frames), and closes what it built; `executor.room_hook(name, trigger)(fn)` defines a room hook by name |
| `ChannelDeclaration` | What the room's owner knows of a channel without its object: `channel_id`, `channel_type`, `category`, `capabilities`, `identity`, `thinks_while_listening`, `recent_events_window`; `channel.declaration()` gives a live channel's |
| `AgentIdentity` | An agent's identity in its declaration: `name`, `role`, `description`, `scope`, `greeting`, `language`, `auto_greet` |
| `DeclaredChannel` | The channel the kit holds for a registered declaration: bound and routed to, never run in the kit's process |
| `TurnClient` | The room owner's side: runs a turn, reads it back as the channel's `ChannelOutput` |
| `OwnerTools` | ABC for the tools a room owner serves its turns: what a request lists, how a call's handler runs |
| `OwnerHost` | ABC for what a room owner runs for its turns' `TurnHost` (`TurnClient(host=)`): `call(request, verb, arguments)`, and `call_between_turns(message)`, refused by default |
| `OwnerEvents` | ABC for where a room owner publishes what its turns published on their executors (`TurnClient(events=)`): `publish(channel, event)`, `emit(...)`, and `reaches_room(room_id, channel_id)`, whose default `False` publishes no turn ephemeral (RFC §8.4) |
| `OwnerTool` | One tool a turn's request lists, served by the room owner (`tool`, `waits_by_design`) |
| `TurnHost` | What a host's tool or hook on a turn's executor asks of the room owner: `send_event`, `delegate`, `wait_task`, `post_status`, `update_room_metadata`, `add_observation` |
| `current_turn_host()` | The `TurnHost` of the turn the current code runs in; after the turn, in work it began, the host for `send_event`, `post_status`, `update_room_metadata`, `add_observation` (`host.open` false); `None` elsewhere |
| `RoomCall` / `RoomPublication` | What an executor sends its room owner after a turn ended (RFC §10.6.3): a host verb, answered by a `HostResult`, and a publication; accepted from the executor of the room's last turn only |
| `RoomOwner` | ABC for what reaches a room owner outside a turn (`room_call`, `room_publication`); `TurnBackend.attend(owner)` has executors reach it |
| `current_turn_id()` | The id of the turn the current code runs in, which `kit.steer(turn_id=...)` addresses; `None` outside a turn |
| `PreviousTurn` | A request's (or a channel call's) `previous_turn`: the room's last turn or channel call of the channel (`turn_id`, `executor_id`), `None` after a detach; an executor drops a room's state another left (RFC §10.6.2) |
| `RoomAttached` / `RoomDetached` | Channel control to the executors that may run the channel's turns (the kit's own alone for a channel it holds live, else every executor declaring it): it calls `on_room_attached` / `on_room_detached` and logs what they raise (RFC §10.6.3) |
| `ChannelCall` / `ChannelResult` | A channel's per-room verb, sent to the executor holding the room's state, and its answer (`result`, `error`, the changed `room_state`) |
| `CommittedEvent` | Channel control to the executor holding the room's state, else one declaring the channel, without moving the holder: it calls `on_room_event(room_id, event)` (a discussion's memory hand-off, RFC §10.6.3) |
| `ChannelControl` | The union of `RoomAttached`, `RoomDetached`, `CommittedEvent` and `ChannelCall` that `TurnBackend.control()` carries |
| `TurnLinkError` | A turn the backend could not carry to its end, its `reason`: `no_executor` (at once when no executor takes the channel, or once the kit's own executor closed for a channel it holds live), `executor_lost`, `frame_lost`, `frame_invalid`, `backend_closed` (a turn backend closed; the executor is not lost) |
| `RemoteTurnError` | An error raised across the turn backend of a class the reading side does not rebuild (outside RoomKit, Python's built-ins and its `error_classes`): keeps the class name (`kind`), its ancestors (`bases`) and its JSON attributes, and is also an instance of the nearest ancestor that side rebuilds (a `ProviderError` subclass still reads as one) |
| `DeliveryResult` | Result of delivering a message |
| `DeliveryStatus` | Delivery status from provider webhook |
